claim: Comparison of seven major AI coding tools: pricing, agentic features, model versions, and decision framework as of June 2026
quote: Seven primary tools dominate the market as of June 2026: Claude Code, Google Antigravity 2.0, OpenAI Codex, Cursor, Kiro, GitHub Copilot, and Windsurf/Devin Desktop

claim: 2026 defines three agent archetypes — CLI-first, IDE-native, and cloud engineering — and the shift from prompts to autonomous execution loops
quote: The biggest change in 2026 is that agents are no longer limited to short prompt-response interactions. They can run for minutes or hours.

claim: Claude Mythos Preview leads SWE-bench Verified at 93.9%; Claude Opus 4.8 at 88.6%; GPT-5.3 Codex at 85%
quote: As of June 2, 2026, Claude Mythos Preview leads the SWE-bench Verified leaderboard with 93.9%, followed by Claude Opus 4.8 (88.6%) and Claude Opus 4.7 (Adaptive) (87.6%).

claim: SWE-bench Verified is contaminated; Claude Opus 4.5 drops 35 points from 80.9% Verified to 45.9% Pro; OpenAI discontinued Verified reporting in early 2026
quote: Claude Opus 4.5 demonstrates the gap: it achieves 80.9% on Verified but only 45.9% on the harder SWE-bench Pro benchmark—a 35-point drop.

claim: Claude Code has 1M token context, strongest for multi-file architectural work; Cursor leads on developer experience with Supermaven 72% autocomplete acceptance
quote: Claude Code's ability to hold up to 1 million tokens in context means it can process an entire mid-sized codebase in a single session

claim: AWS Kiro launched May 7 2026 replacing Amazon Q Developer; uses spec-driven development with requirements.md, design.md, tasks.md; parallel task execution cuts time by 75%
quote: Parallel Task Execution runs independent coding tasks concurrently rather than sequentially, cutting implementation times for large projects by roughly 75 percent.

claim: Gemini CLI is open source (Apache 2.0) with free tier: 60 req/min, 1000 req/day, 1M token context with Gemini 3 models
quote: Gemini CLI is an open-source AI agent that brings the power of Gemini directly into your terminal.

claim: Gemini CLI open-source repo with 105k stars, built in TypeScript
quote: An open-source AI agent that brings the power of Gemini directly into your terminal.

claim: OpenAI Codex CLI open-source repo with 90k stars
quote: A lightweight coding agent that runs in your terminal.

claim: Claude Code open-source repo with 131k stars
quote: Claude Code is an agentic coding tool made by Anthropic.

claim: Cognition acquired Windsurf, shipped SWE-1.5/1.6 (13x faster than Claude Sonnet 4.5); Codemaps add AI-annotated visual code navigation; Windsurf rebranded as Devin Desktop June 2026
quote: Cognition shipped a proprietary coding model called SWE-1.5 that the company claims is 13x faster than Claude Sonnet 4.5.

claim: MCP has 97M monthly SDK downloads, 10K+ public servers, 41% of surveyed orgs in production; donated to Linux Foundation in Dec 2025
quote: By March 2026, MCP had achieved 97 million monthly downloads of the Python and TypeScript SDKs, 10,000+ active public MCP servers.

claim: Augment Code has 200K-token Context Engine with 70.6% SWE-bench Verified (self-reported); highest accuracy on public AI code review benchmark
quote: Augment Code is an enterprise-focused AI coding agent built around a 200K-token Context Engine with strong SWE-bench Verified results (70.6% self-reported)

claim: Aider is an open-source CLI coding assistant with 46k GitHub stars
quote: Aider lets you pair program with LLMs, to edit code in your local git repository.

claim: Cline is an open-source VS Code extension with 63k GitHub stars that can inspect projects, edit files, run terminal commands, and use a browser
quote: Autonomous coding agent right in your IDE, capable of creating/editing files, executing commands, using the browser, and more.

claim: Kiro is AWS's agentic IDE for spec-driven development with MCP integration, routing between Claude Sonnet and Amazon Nova via Bedrock
quote: Kiro is an agentic coding service that works alongside you to turn prompts into detailed specs, then into working code, docs, and tests.

claim: AWS added Requirements Analysis to Kiro to mathematically prove requirements are contradiction-free before code generation, targeting 'AI slop'
quote: AWS is adding a Requirements Analysis feature designed to mathematically prove that software requirements are free of contradictions and gaps before any code gets written

claim: Coding agents span four categories: IDE extensions, dedicated IDEs, CLI tools, and cloud platforms; many tools span multiple categories
quote: The agents are classified into four types: IDE extensions (GitHub Copilot, Cline, Continue), Dedicated IDEs (Cursor, Windsurf, Zed), CLI tools (Claude Code, Aider, Gemini CLI), Cloud platforms (Devin, OpenHands, Jules)
